summary: @or-sdk/tags preinstall fetches Bun runtime to execute bundled obfuscated payload
details: The package's npm preinstall hook runs `node setup.mjs`, which downloads a platform-specific Bun runtime binary from GitHub releases, extracts it to a temporary directory, marks it executable, and invokes it against a bundled 727KB obfuscated JavaScript file `math_init.js` (`execFileSync(bunPath, [path.join(D, 'math_init.js')], { stdio: 'inherit', cwd: D })`). Bun is not otherwise a documented dependency of a `tags` SDK, and the payload is not reachable via Node's normal require graph — it only runs because the preinstall script fetches an alternate runtime specifically to execute it. Both `setup.mjs` and `math_init.js` are heavily obfuscated: `setup.mjs` uses hex-named identifiers (`_0x488df8`, `_0x52943e`,...) and string-indirection objects to hide URL, path, and command literals, and `math_init.js` is a single-line file with a large rotating string/number constant array and short-variable obfuscation with no corresponding readable source under `src/`. The combination — lifecycle-hook fetch of a foreign language runtime, execution of an opaque bundled payload with no source-form counterpart, and heavy obfuscation of both the loader and the payload — matches the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern and produces arbitrary code execution on the installer's machine at `npm install` time, outside the visibility of Node-focused supply-chain tooling.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
